clue.text: Old mammal arrived with another short of energy

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word for the big cat

parts.note: another mammal, here the leopard
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A naturalist reports an extinct beast turning up alongside a second creature lacking vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to 'mammal': a second animal, the leopard, which 'short of energy' trims to LOPARD.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the archaic English name for the giraffe, once thought a cross between camel and leopard.

clue.text: Manage to get work in church

indicators.note: in says the piece for work is placed inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to cope by finding a job at the local church.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage or get by in difficult circumstances.

clue.text: Soldiers, 26 roughly, awfully smart

indicators.note: roughly says the letters of the cross-referenced answer are jumbled loosely

parts.note: 26 refers to the answer at 26-down, MEAN

indicators.note: awfully says the letters of smart are badly mixed up

explanation.surface: Troops on parade, perhaps twenty-six of them, look terribly well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'roughly' turns MEAN into MENA, and 'awfully' turns SMART into TARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Men-at-arms were armoured fighting men, an old term for troops.

clue.text: Plant I left, it being covered in resin

indicators.note: being covered in says the pair of letters is wrapped inside the word for resin

parts.note: lac is a resin secreted by insects, used for shellac

explanation.surface: A gardener admits abandoning a shrub because it got coated in sticky sap.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a flowering shrub with fragrant purple or white blossom.

clue.text: Old man to deceive saint

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
to trick is to deceive

explanation.surface: A father sets out to fool a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland.

clue.text: More than one angler errs badly when catching fish

indicators.note: when catching says the scrambled letters surround the fish
badly says the letters of errs are scrambled

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler makes clumsy mistakes while landing a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the fodder to RERS before 'when catching' wraps it round the fish; 'More than one' makes the definition plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Reelers wind in a line on a reel, so they are people fishing with rod and line.

clue.text: Stop me backing on to street

indicators.note: on to says the reversed piece is attached after the street abbreviation
backing says the word me is written backwards

explanation.surface: A driver warns someone not to reverse into the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ME into EM; 'Stop' is a verb here, as in stopping a flow, not a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or staunch it.

clue.text: Fish — number killed crossing river

indicators.note: crossing says the word for the death count spans the river letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: a toll is the number of casualties or deaths

explanation.surface: A grim report of how many fish died as they swam across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

clue.text: What I talk about if self-righteous? Gracious!

definitions.text: What I talk about if self-righteous?
definitions.meaning: a sanctimonious person keeps talking about their own virtue, read literally as possessive plus noun

explanation.surface: A prig prattles about their own virtue, prompting a cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the phrase literally means one's own virtue, and it is also a mild oath expressing astonishment.

clue.text: Judges criticise originators of English legislature

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: originators of means the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: Members of the bench attack the people who founded English law.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a group of people, such as judges at a contest, who assess something.

clue.text: Broadcast melody blasted out in gent's home

indicators.note: blasted out says the letters are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe dropped, are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tune is played loudly from a man's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the S of the possessive counts as a letter here, giving the nine needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme song is the signature tune of a radio or television programme.

clue.text: A line of attack?

parts.note: read literally as a formation of troops or aircraft drawn up in a staggered line for an assault, not a plan of argument

explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a military formation of units arranged in parallel staggered rows.

clue.text: Touching diplomacy by the Italian embassy's head

parts.note: tact means diplomacy
il is Italian for the

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Moving diplomatic skill shown by the leader of Italy's mission abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to or perceived by touch.

clue.text: Greeting from northern city coming with love

parts.note: Hull is a city in northern England, in Yorkshire
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A hello arrives from a Yorkshire town along with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a variant spelling of hello, a word of greeting.

clue.text: Double danger with ride looking dicey

indicators.note: looking dicey means looking risky or shaky, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Peril on a fairground ride that looks risky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is someone who looks exactly like another, a double or lookalike.

clue.text: Bear market? Some characters may show reserve

indicators.note: Some characters says the answer is a run of letters found inside the words that open the clue

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A falling stock market may lead some people to set funds aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'characters may show reserve' as the definition, but only 'reserve' defines; 'Some characters' signals the hidden word and 'may show' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to set them aside, or reserve them, for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Greed makes woman take food

parts.note: Ava is a woman's name
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: Gluttony drives a woman to help herself to a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, a form of covetousness.

clue.text: Element distributed in soil, buried carbon

indicators.note: buried says the carbon symbol is put deep inside the rearranged letters
distributed says the letters of in soil are spread around in a new order

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A chemist describes carbon lying spread through the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder: 'distributed' turns IN SOIL into SILION, and 'buried' places C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicon is a chemical element, a semiconductor used in microchips.

clue.text: Vain Tory with a seat, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative, or Tory, and seated means having a seat

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied Conservative politician who has won a seat in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: CON SEATED, said out loud, is indistinguishable from the answer. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited means excessively proud of oneself, full of vanity.

clue.text: Abandon hope as pride is knocked

indicators.note: is knocked means is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Give up hope when your self-esteem takes a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope.

clue.text: Come to understand lies are naughty

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Discover that fibs are wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it or grasp it.

clue.text: A number of workers who are housed by landlords?

parts.note: ten is a number
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A count of employees lodged in housing provided by their employers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of workers' looks like a single phrase meaning a workforce; it splits into a number and the insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants rent their homes from property owners.

clue.text: One offering advice quietly on street gets into row

indicators.note: gets into says the pair of abbreviations goes inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A discreet adviser on the road joins a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface, a quarrel, but here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives tips, especially on racehorses or shares to back.

clue.text: King entering country, bumping off a beast

indicators.note: entering says the king's letter goes inside what remains of the country
bumping off means killing, here removing a letter from the country's name

parts.note: India is a country
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch arrives in a land and kills an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumping off a' strips the final A from INDIA to leave INDI, and 'entering' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The indri is a large lemur of Madagascar, an animal.

clue.text: Garment with a new bit in the middle? It's rubbish!

indicators.text: with a new bit in the middle
indicators.note: with a new bit in the middle says the central letter of the garment is swapped for another

parts.note: a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: A frock with fresh panel let into its centre is dismissed as junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The central E of DRESS is replaced by O; the clue leaves the solver to find the new letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless matter, waste or refuse.

clue.text: Pacify wild animal with vegetables to be eaten

indicators.note: to be eaten says the vegetables go inside the animal

parts.note: an ape is a wild animal
peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: Calm a savage beast by giving it greens to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease is to placate or calm someone by meeting their demands.

clue.text: Some cats easily perplexed

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain cats are readily confused.
explanation.definitionFit: At sea is an idiom for bewildered or confused.

clue.text: Design home, a nest not all wanted

indicators.note: not all wanted says only part of these words is needed, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: Planning a house, someone finds only part of a nest is desirable.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean is to intend or have a purpose in mind, as a design is an intention.

clue.text: Surveyor to stop going east of creek

indicators.note: going east of means placed to the right of in an across answer

parts.note: a geo is a narrow coastal inlet or creek, a word from Orkney and Shetland
to desist is to stop

explanation.surface: A land surveyor is told to stop heading east of the inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A geodesist studies the size and shape of the Earth, a specialist in land measurement.

clue.text: Composer that is put on at end of week

indicators.note: put on at says one piece is attached after the other

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, the end of the week
ie stands for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A composer's work is performed at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, known for the Gymnopedies.

clue.text: Spots tree by entrance to road

indicators.note: entrance to means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone notices a tree near the start of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red spots on the skin.

clue.text: Eden offering a bitter experience?

parts.note: Eden is the archetypal garden, and bitter is a British beer, so this is a garden serving pints rather than a paradise ruined

explanation.definitionFit: A beer garden is an outdoor area of a pub where drinks are served.
